definition: Self-understanding is a person’s clearer awareness of their own inner motives, reactions, and patterns of meaning, including influences outside conscious awareness. In psychodynamic work, it is valued as part of making sense of what is unconscious.

provenance.scope: Source record D064889; pinned source text

reasons: The packet is a MeSH descriptor for “Psychotherapy, Psychodynamic,” not a definition of the term “self-understanding,” so the requested sense is not supported.
The definition adds specific claims about “inner motives, reactions, and patterns of meaning” and “influences outside conscious awareness” that are not stated in the packet.

“In psychodynamic work” is broader and more specific than the packet’s wording; the packet supports only that psychodynamic psychotherapy places a premium on self-understanding and making meaning of what is unconscious.

The definition claims that self-understanding involves “clearer awareness” of “inner motives, reactions, and patterns of meaning,” but the packet only states that psychodynamic/psychoanalytic psychotherapy has a “premium on self understanding and making meaning of what is unconscious,” without detailing motives/reactions/patterns of meaning.

The definition states that this includes “influences outside conscious awareness.” The packet supports reacting to “unconscious forces” but does not explicitly phrase self-understanding as including influences “outside conscious awareness.”
The definition’s first sentence contains substantive specifics not present in the packet; only the general link between self-understanding and making meaning of what is unconscious is supported.
